original: WPRPLACE, formerly Ben Boyd National Park, is a national park in New South Wales, Australia, 578 km south of Sydney. It was established in 1971 and officially renamed in [dated source] owing to its previous namesake's connection with blackbirding. Beowa means "orca", an animal of significance to the traditional owners, the Thaua people.
